title: Cusa–Huygens-type inequality for generalized hyperbolic functions
statement:
Let $p\in(2,\infty)$ and $x\in(0,\pi_p/2)$, where $\sinh_p$ and $\cos_p$ are the generalized hyperbolic sine and trigonometric cosine functions, respectively, and $\pi_p$ is the associated constant. Then

$$
\frac{\sinh_p(x)}{x}<\frac{p+1}{p+\cos_p(x)}.
$$

**Cusa–Huygens-type conjecture.** The displayed inequality holds for every $p\in(2,\infty)$ and every $x\in(0,\pi_p/2)$. This is part of a sequence of Cusa–Huygens-type inequalities for generalized functions; the supplied text gives no resolution or further evidence for this parameter range.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.6749

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2012).
source_name: Riku Klén, Matti Vuorinen and Xiaohui Zhang, “Inequalities for the generalized trigonometric and hyperbolic functions”, arXiv:1210.6749 (2012).
